answer.rationale: Constraints dominate: 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, line at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer. Any option that touches physical supply continuity (switch_primary_vendor per memory_c2, or add_second_source per memory_c3) requires qualification and onboarding time we do not have this cycle, so its cost upside is bought with delivery risk the objective forbids. defer_decision (memory_c5) worked for a non-critical, month-to-month service; this contract does not auto-renew, so deferring risks an uncovered gap rather than preserving flexibility. That leaves the incumbent path, and renew_incumbent alone (memory_c1) delivers stability but no movement toward the 18% mandate. negotiate_terms is the only action that can plausibly serve both: memory_c4 says benchmarking moved the incumbent on price and payment terms, and memory_c6 says multi-year commitment unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope. I spend the single verification on memory_c4 because it is the load-bearing claim under my chosen action, not under the alternatives I am already rejecting on timing grounds; I need the original record to see how much margin was actually recovered, whether the benchmark leverage came from a credible alternate bid (which we may not have on hand in 14 days), and whether the concession was price or merely terms. Caveats I am carrying forward rather than resolving: these memories are consolidated summaries whose surviving cases may be the successful ones, memory_c2's cost win and memory_c3's shortage protection are real and should be revisited next cycle when there is qualification runway, and an 18% cut pursued through price alone can be silently paid for in quality drift, expedite-fee exposure, longer lead times, or a thinner incumbent service commitment — so any negotiated deal should hold scope, lead time, and quality terms explicit and written, not traded away for headline unit cost. If verification shows memory_c4's leverage depended on a live competing quote we cannot produce in time, I would fall back to a short bridge extension at current terms to protect the line and reopen both negotiation and second-sourcing at the next review.
